children: Sterling rises after data showed an unexpected decline in the U.K. unemployment rate for the three months to August. The unemployment rate fell to 4.7% from 4.9% in the previous three months. Economists in a WSJ survey had expected the rate to remain at 4.9%. Average earnings excluding bonuses rose at faster pace of 3.7% for the quarter, against an expected 3.6%. The data cement expectations that the Bank of England could raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting in November. Sterling rises 0.3% to an intraday high of $1.3348 after the data, from $1.3329 beforehand. The euro falls 0.2% to an intraday low of 0.8410 pounds, from 0.8422 beforehand. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
